{{Short description|Mathematical arithmetic dynamics function}}

{{sources exist|date=July 2024}}

In [[arithmetic dynamics]], an '''arboreal Galois representation''' is a [[Continuous function|continuous]] [[group homomorphism]] between the [[absolute Galois group]] of a field and the [[automorphism group]] of an infinite, regular, rooted [[tree (graph theory)|tree]].

The study of arboreal Galois representations of goes back to the works of Odoni in 1980s.

== Definition ==

Let <math>K</math> be a [[field (mathematics)|field]] and <math>K^{sep}</math> be its [[separable closure]]. The [[Galois group]] <math>G_K</math> of the extension <math>K^{sep}/K</math> is called the [[absolute Galois group]] of <math>K</math>. This is a [[profinite group]] and it is therefore endowed with its natural Krull topology.

For a positive integer <math>d</math>, let <math>T^d</math> be the infinite regular rooted [[tree (graph theory)|tree]] of degree <math>d</math>. This is an infinite tree where one node is labeled as the root of the tree and every node has exactly <math>d</math> descendants. An '''automorphism''' of <math>T^d</math> is a bijection of the set of nodes that preserves vertex-edge connectivity. The group <math>Aut(T^d)</math> of all automorphisms of <math>T^d</math> is a profinite group as well, as it can be seen as the [[inverse limit]] of the automorphism groups of the finite sub-trees <math>T^d_n</math> formed by all nodes at distance at most <math>n</math> from the root. The group of automorphisms of <math>T^d_n</math> is isomorphic to <math>S_d\wr S_d\wr \ldots \wr S_d</math>, the iterated [[wreath product]] of <math>n</math> copies of the [[symmetric group]] of degree <math>d</math>.

An arboreal Galois representation is a [[Continuous function#Continuous functions between topological spaces|continuous]] [[group homomorphism]] <math>G_K \to Aut(T^d)</math>.

== Arboreal Galois representations attached to rational functions ==
The most natural source of arboreal Galois representations is the theory of iterations of self-[[rational functions]] on the [[projective line]]. Let <math>K</math> be a [[field (mathematics)|field]] and <math>f \colon \mathbb P^1_K\to \mathbb P^1_K</math> a rational function of degree <math>d</math>. For every <math>n\geq 1</math> let <math>f^n=f\circ f\circ \ldots \circ f</math> be the <math>n</math>-fold composition of the map <math>f</math> with itself. Let <math>\alpha\in K</math> and suppose that for every <math>n\geq 1</math> the set <math>(f^n)^{-1}(\alpha)</math> contains <math>d^n</math> elements of the [[algebraic closure]] <math>\overline{K}</math>. Then one can construct an infinite, regular, rooted <math>d</math>-ary tree <math>T(f)</math> in the following way: the root of the tree is <math>\alpha</math>, and the [[Vertex (graph theory)|nodes]] at distance <math>n</math> from <math>\alpha</math> are the elements of <math>(f^n)^{-1}(\alpha)</math>. A node <math>\beta</math> at distance <math>n</math> from <math>\alpha</math> is connected with an edge to a node <math>\gamma</math> at distance <math>n+1</math> from <math>\alpha</math> if and only if <math>f(\beta)=\gamma</math>.

[[File:PreimageTree.png|thumb|The first three levels of the tree of preimages of <math>0</math> under the map <math>x^2+1</math>]]

The absolute Galois group <math>G_K</math> [[Group action|acts]] on <math>T(f)</math> via automorphisms, and the induced homomorphism <math>\rho_{f,\alpha}\colon G_K\to Aut(T(f))</math> is continuous, and therefore is called the arboreal Galois representation attached to <math>f</math> with basepoint <math>\alpha</math>.

Arboreal representations attached to rational functions can be seen as a wide generalization of [[Galois module|Galois representations]] on [[Tate module|Tate modules]] of [[abelian variety|abelian varieties]].

== Arboreal Galois representations attached to quadratic polynomials ==

The simplest non-trivial case is that of monic quadratic polynomials. Let <math>K</math> be a field of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] not 2, let <math>f=(x-a)^2+b\in K[x]</math> and set the basepoint <math>\alpha=0</math>. The '''adjusted post-critical orbit''' of <math>f</math> is the sequence defined by <math>c_1=-f(a)</math> and <math>c_n= f^n(a)</math> for every <math>n\geq 2</math>. A resultant argument<ref>{{cite journal |last=Jones | first=Rafe | title=The density of prime divisors in the arithmetic dynamics of quadratic polynomials| journal=  Journal of the London Mathematical Society| volume=78 |number=2| year=2008 | pages= 523–544| doi=10.1112/jlms/jdn034 | arxiv=math/0612415 | s2cid=15310955 }}</ref> shows that <math>(f^n)^{-1}(0)</math> has <math>d^n</math> elements for ever <math>n</math> if and only if <math>c_n\neq 0</math> for every <math>n</math>. In 1992, Stoll proved the following theorem:<ref name="Stoll">{{cite journal |last=Stoll | first=Michael | title= Galois groups over <math>cQ</math> of some iterated polynomials| journal= Archiv der Mathematik| volume=59 | number = 3| year=1992 | pages= 239–244| doi=10.1007/BF01197321 | s2cid=122514918 }}</ref>

:'''Theorem''': the arboreal representation <math>\rho_{f,0}</math> is surjective if and only if the [[Linear span|span]] of <math>\{c_1,\ldots,c_n\}</math> in the <math>\mathbb F_2</math>-[[vector space]] <math>K^*/(K^*)^2</math> is <math>n</math>-dimensional for every <math>n\geq 1</math>.

The following are examples of polynomials that satisfy the conditions of Stoll's Theorem, and that therefore have surjective arboreal representations.

* For <math>K=\mathbb Q</math>, <math>f=x^2+a</math>, where <math>a\in \mathbb Z</math> is such that either <math>a>0</math> and <math>a\equiv 1,2\bmod 4</math> or <math>a<0</math>, <math>a\equiv 0\bmod 4</math> and <math>-a</math> is not a square. <ref name="Stoll" />

* Let <math>k</math> be a field of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] not <math>2</math> and <math>K=k(t)</math> be the rational function field over <math>k</math>. Then <math>f=x^2+t\in K[x]</math> has surjective arboreal representation.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ferraguti|first1=Andrea|last2=Micheli|first2=Giacomo|title= An equivariant isomorphism theorem for mod <math>\mathfrak p</math> reductions of arboreal Galois representations| journal = Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.| number=12|volume=373|pages=8525–8542|year=2020|doi=10.1090/tran/8247 |arxiv=1905.00506}}</ref>

== Higher degrees and Odoni's conjecture ==

In 1985 Odoni formulated the following conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal |last= Odoni| first= R.W.K.|title=The Galois theory of iterates and composites of polynomials|journal= Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society|volume= 51 |year=1985| number=3|pages=385–414| doi= 10.1112/plms/s3-51.3.385}}</ref>

:'''Conjecture''': Let <math>K</math> be a [[Hilbertian field]] of characteristic <math>0</math>, and let <math>n</math> be a positive integer. Then there exists a polynomial <math>f\in K[x]</math> of degree <math>n</math> such that <math>\rho_{f,0}</math> is surjective.

Although in this very general form the conjecture has been shown to be false by Dittmann and Kadets,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dittmann |first1= Philip | last2= Kadets| first2= Borys| title= Odoni's conjecture on arboreal Galois representations is false.| journal= Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.| volume= 150| number = 8| pages=3335–3343| year =2022|doi= 10.1090/proc/15920 | arxiv= 2012.03076}}</ref> there are several results when <math>K</math> is a [[number field]]. Benedetto and Juul proved Odoni's conjecture for <math>K</math> a number field and <math>n</math> even, and also when both <math>[K:\mathbb Q]</math> and <math>n</math> are odd,<ref>{{cite journal| last1= Benedetto|first1= Robert|last2=Juul|first2= Jamie| title=Odoni's conjecture for number fields|journal= Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|volume=51|number=2|pages=237–250|year=2019|doi= 10.1112/blms.12225|arxiv= 1803.01987|s2cid= 53400216}}</ref> Looper independently proved Odoni's conjecture for <math>n</math> prime and <math>K=\mathbb Q</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Looper|first=Nicole|title= Dynamical Galois groups of trinomials and Odoni's conjecture|journal= Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|volume=51|number=2|pages=278–292|year=2019|doi=10.1112/blms.12227 |arxiv=1609.03398}}</ref>

== Finite index conjecture ==

When <math>K</math> is a [[global field]] and <math>f\in K(x)</math> is a rational function of degree 2, the image of <math>\rho_{f,0}</math> is expected to be "large" in most cases. The following conjecture quantifies the previous statement, and it was formulated by Jones in 2013.<ref>{{cite book |last=Jones | first=Rafe | title= Galois representations from pre-image trees: an arboreal survey.|series=Actes de la Conférence ''Théorie des Nombres et Applications''|year=2013 | pages= 107–136}}</ref>

:'''Conjecture''' Let <math>K</math> be a global field and <math>f\in K(x)</math> a rational function of degree 2. Let <math>\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in \mathbb P^1_K</math> be the [[critical point (mathematics)|critical points]] of <math>f</math>. Then <math>[Aut(T(f)):Im(\rho_{f,0})]=\infty</math> if and only if at least one of the following conditions hold:
# The map <math>f</math> is [[post-critically finite]], namely the orbits of <math>\gamma_1,\gamma_2</math> are both finite.
# There exists <math>n\geq 1</math> such that <math>f^n(\gamma_1)=f^n(\gamma_2)</math>.
# <math>0</math> is a [[periodic point]] for <math>f</math>.
# There exist a [[Möbius transformation]] <math>m=\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}\in PGL_2(K)</math> that fixes <math>0</math> and is such that <math>m\circ f \circ m^{-1}=f</math>.

Jones' conjecture is considered to be a dynamical analogue of Serre's open image theorem.

One direction of Jones' conjecture is known to be true: if <math>f</math> satisfies one of the above conditions, then <math>[Aut(T(f)):Im(\rho_{f,0})]=\infty</math>. In particular, when <math>f</math> is post-critically finite then <math>Im(\rho_{f,\alpha})</math> is a topologically finitely generated closed subgroup of <math>Aut(T(f))</math> for every <math>\alpha\in K</math>.

In the other direction, Juul et al. proved that if the [[abc conjecture]] holds for number fields, <math>K</math> is a [[number field]] and <math>f\in K[x]</math> is a quadratic polynomial, then <math>[Aut(T(f)):Im(\rho_{f,0})]=\infty</math> if and only if <math>f</math> is [[post-critically finite]] or not [[Eventually stable polynomial|eventually stable]]. When <math>f\in K[x]</math> is a quadratic polynomial, conditions (2) and (4) in Jones' conjecture are never satisfied. Moreover, Jones and Levy conjectured that <math>f</math> is [[Eventually stable polynomial|eventually stable]] if and only if <math>0</math> is not periodic for <math>f</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jones|first1=Rafe|last2=Levy|first2=Alon|title=Eventually stable rational functions|journal= Int. J. Number Theory|volume=13|number=9|pages=2299–2318|year=2017|doi=10.1142/S1793042117501263 |arxiv=1603.00673 |s2cid=119704204 }}</ref>

== Abelian arboreal representations==

In 2020, Andrews and Petsche formulated the following conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Andrews|first1=Jesse|last2=Petsche|first2=Clayton|title=Abelian extensions in dynamical Galois theory|journal=Algebra Number Theory|volume=14|number=7|pages=1981–1999|year=2020|doi=10.2140/ant.2020.14.1981 |arxiv=2001.00659 |s2cid=209832399 }}</ref>

:'''Conjecture''' Let <math>K</math> be a [[number field]], let <math>f \in K[x]</math> be a polynomial of degree <math>d\ge 2</math> and let <math>\alpha\in K</math>. Then <math>Im(\rho_{f,\alpha})</math> is abelian if and only if there exists a [[root of unity]] <math>\zeta</math> such that the pair <math>(f,\alpha)</math> is conjugate over the [[maximal abelian extension]] <math>K^{ab}</math> to <math>(x^d,\zeta)</math> or to <math>(\pm T_d,\zeta+\zeta^{-1})</math>, where <math>T_d</math> is the [[Chebyshev polynomial|Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind]] of degree <math>d</math>.

Two pairs <math>(f,\alpha),(g,\beta)</math>, where <math>f,g\in K(x)</math> and <math>\alpha,\beta\in K</math> are '''conjugate''' over a field extension <math>L/K</math> if there exists a [[Möbius transformation]] <math>m=\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}\in PGL_2(L)</math> such that <math>m\circ f \circ m^{-1}=g</math> and <math>m(\alpha)=\beta</math>. Conjugacy is an [[equivalence relation]]. The Chebyshev polynomials the conjecture refers to are a normalized version, conjugate by the [[Möbius transformation]] <math>2x</math> to make them monic.

It has been proven that Andrews and Petsche's conjecture holds true when <math>K=\mathbb Q</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ferraguti|first1=Andrea|last2=Ostafe|first2=Alina|last3=Zannier|first3=Umberto|title=Cyclotomic and abelian points in backward orbits of rational functions|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|volume=438|year=2024|article-number=109463 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2023.109463 |arxiv=2203.10034 |s2cid=247594240 }}</ref>
